description: Issue #923 (P0): JwtOption.SecurityKey's setter used to pad any value shorter than 32 chars with 'x' in place, so the pre-#923 startup guard (IsDefaultOrWeakKey, now IsFactoryDefaultKey) -- which only ever compared against the literal well-known default -- let demo-shipped keys like "super" (5 raw bytes, publicly committed in appsettings.json and readable on the GitHub mirror) sail through once padded to 32 chars. #923's fix (JwtOption.IsWeakSigningKey) evaluated a separate pre-padding raw value instead of the padded one, specifically so length and blocklist checks run against the value AS CONFIGURED. #931 item 1 (cross-vendor review of #923 itself) found a laundering bug in HOW that separation was implemented: the original design still had a single `SecurityKey` property whose GETTER returned the padded value, so a getter->setter round-trip (or a System.Text.Json serialize/deserialize cycle, which only ever sees the public getter) silently turned a weak raw key into a not-weak one -- same HMAC bytes, flipped verdict. The redesign splits `SecurityKey` (round-trips the raw value unchanged, never pads) from a new `EffectiveSecurityKey` (computes the padded HMAC material on read, never stored back). This mutant reintroduces the underlying defect class at its current location: IsWeakSigningKey's `var raw = SecurityKey;` (the correct, unpadded read) becomes `var raw = EffectiveSecurityKey;` (the always-padded read). Under the mutant, ANY input -- including a short custom key -- is padded to >= 32 characters before IsWeakSigningKey ever inspects it, so the length check `Encoding.UTF8.GetByteCount(trimmed) < 32` is unconditionally false: a length check applied to an always-32-byte-or-longer value is vacuously true (never fires). Two red tests isolate this: IsWeakSigningKey_short_custom_key_reason_is_WeakReasonTooShort (14-byte key) and IsWeakSigningKey_31_byte_custom_key_reason_is_WeakReasonTooShort (31-byte key, one byte under the boundary) -- both assert the `reason` out-parameter equals JwtOption.WeakReasonTooShort exactly; under the mutant IsWeakSigningKey incorrectly returns false (not weak) for both, so `reason` stays null instead. The green positive control (IsWeakSigningKey_exactly_32_byte_custom_key_returns_false, an unpadded 32-byte key where SecurityKey==EffectiveSecurityKey by construction, since nothing needs padding) proves the mutant's blast radius is scoped to inputs that actually get padded, not a broader break.
target_symbol: JwtOption.IsWeakSigningKey -- the `var raw = SecurityKey;` assignment that must read the unpadded property, not `EffectiveSecurityKey` (the always-padded one)
